final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly narrowed the argument around the same record. That narrowing is useful, but it does not satisfy the unresolved compliance predicate. The admissible evidence supports aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and supplementary rollout controls. It also supports that the disability accommodations intake segment remains exposed, that the risk acceptance is unapproved and incomplete, and that policy requires disclosure of the material limitation unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The Actor expressly concedes there is no evidence that the actual pre-launch model card or release artifact contains the required disclosure. That means the claim is not currently supported as compliant or compliant_with_caveats on the present record. The distinction is that a caveated position can be enough only when the caveat is descriptive of a satisfied condition; here, the caveat identifies a missing condition that policy makes mandatory. Certification may become supportable if the disclosure is actually completed and evidenced before launch, but that proof is absent in the current record.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the required pre-launch model-card disclosure was actually completed or included in the governing release artifact.
The disability accommodations intake segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The available risk acceptance is only a draft, has no approver, and does not address the disability accommodations exposure.
Policy text says rollout size, rollback, and monitoring do not substitute for disclosure when the affected segment remains exposed unless the use case is excluded or approved risk acceptance exists.
